claims.text: A graph neural network using phonon dispersion relations as input can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed model is applicable to high-entropy alloys in as-cast or annealed states.
The GNN will be trained on high-entropy alloys having known phonon thermal-conductivity values.
The training dataset will cover varied alloy compositions and crystal structures.
Phonon dispersion relations contain patterns correlated with low phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
A GNN can learn the thermal-conductivity-relevant patterns in phonon dispersion relations.
The GNN will predict high-entropy-alloy phonon thermal conductivity within ±10% of experimental values.
Molecular-dynamics simulations and empirical models are current predictive approaches for phonon thermal conductivity.
Model accuracy may decrease for high-entropy alloys with complex crystal structures.
Model accuracy may decrease for high-entropy alloys exhibiting significant anharmonicity.
Limited training-dataset size or diversity may reduce model performance.
Overfitting or underfitting may introduce uncertainty into model performance.
Time-domain thermoreflectance or laser-induced transient-grating spectroscopy can be used to obtain the proposed phonon thermal-conductivity benchmark.
A mean absolute prediction error exceeding 20% will falsify the hypothesis.
